Maya Singh: Urgent — while at a customer site in Lima I unexpectedly fractured my ankle and the local hospital says I need a medevac repatriation to the UK. They've requested a deposit and quoted an air ambulance. I paid the hospital deposit on my card to avoid delay. What documentation do you need to process the evacuation and any upfront costs?
Maria (People Ops): Oh no, hope you're ok. First priority is medical care and safety. For expenses: attach the hospital invoice, proof of payment, medevac quote/invoice, correspondence from the provider, and any police/incident reports if applicable. We'll coordinate with our travel insurance and security.
Dr. Kline (Health & Safety): If the medevac is clinically indicated, we cover coordination and the company will work with our insurance partner to arrange repatriation. Please keep copies of all medical records (discharge summaries, physician note confirming evacuation necessity). Redact sensitive details except diagnosis and treatment summary.
Maya Singh: I have the hospital invoice and paid £1,200 deposit. The medevac provider emailed a provisional quote of £18,000. I attached screenshots in Expensely for now.
security-bot: Security alert logged. Contacted duty officer in APAC and pinged our local security rep. If you need an escort or airport assistance, reply here.
travel-insurance-bot: Policy X-893 triggered. Please provide claimant name, passport number (redacted in upload), incident date, and all provider invoices. We will open the claim and advise on direct-bill vs reimbursement.
Sam Patel (Finance): Finance note: if insurance pays directly, AP will process the net. If you paid upfront, submit a reimbursement request with proof_of_payment.pdf, itemized_invoices.pdf, and manager_approval.pdf. For medevac, Finance will fast-track but need the insurance claim ID if available.
Maya Singh: Manager approved emergency assistance (Liam Chen). He texted "approved emergency medevac" and asked me to proceed. I also took photos of injury and hospital stamp.
Maria (People Ops): Good. Upload manager text or approval email as manager_approval.pdf. Also include authorization from attending physician that medevac is necessary for repatriation. That speeds insurance pre-approval.
Dr. Kline (Health & Safety): If air ambulance is refused by insurer we may need to consider scheduled commercial stretcher or accompanying medical escort; keep all alternative quotes. Capture timestamps on each communication.
Maya Singh: One question: are incidental travel costs for my spouse (who flew to accompany me) covered? They bought a refundable economy ticket and paid hotel for the night before repatriation.
Maria (People Ops): Spouse/partner travel is covered only in emergency evacuation cases where company security approves an accompanying person. If security/team approved, submit spouse's receipts (flight, hotel) with a note from security confirming approval. We will coordinate with insurance for direct billing when possible.
Sam Patel (Finance): For coding in Expensely (copy/paste):
```
Expense type: "Emergency Medical - Medevac & Hospital"
Project/Cost center: "People Ops - Employee Care"
GL account: "6300 - Medical & Emergency Assistance"
Description: "Medevac repatriation and hospital deposit for Maya Singh (Lima). Insurance claim ID: <leave blank if unknown>. Manager approval attached."
Required attachments: hospital_invoice.pdf, proof_of_payment.pdf, medevac_quote.pdf, physician_note.pdf, manager_approval.pdf, security_approval.pdf, spouse_receipts.pdf (if applicable)
```
Sam Patel (Finance): Note: if you uploaded screenshots, please replace with official PDFs or emailed invoices. Finance needs itemized invoices (not just screenshots of totals).
Maya Singh: The medevac company said insurer pre-approval takes 24-48h. They recommended immediate deposit to secure flight. I paid deposit on my card.
travel-insurance-bot: Upload provided docs to claim portal within 48 hours. If deposit paid, insurer may reimburse. Keep original receipts and any wire receipts.
Maria (People Ops): Also flag People Ops on the claim if the cost is over £5k so we can coordinate approvals and expedite payment.
Dr. Kline (Health & Safety): After repatriation, please upload the final discharge summary and any follow-up treatment invoices. We'll also review duty-of-care actions and whether additional support (rehab, counseling) is needed.
Maya Singh: Safety question: will I be expected to use paid leave while recovering or is medical leave auto-approved for evacuation events?
Maria (People Ops): Medical leave policy applies. Submit medical certificate/fit note. For the immediate period, we'll put you on emergency paid medical leave and coordinate long-term leave with you. HR will reach out separately.
Sam Patel (Finance): Final procedural note: if a refund comes from the medevac provider (e.g., partial chargeback) notify AP immediately. We reconcile reimbursements against actual insurer payouts.
Maya Singh: Thanks everyone. Uploading docs now. Appreciate the rapid help. :pray:
